body:
Priya S: FYI customer (acme-ml-app) raising an escalation: SSE streams show partial final chunks after short network blips. When client reconnects the lost tail appears as a separate event (duplicate tokens) and sometimes the stream ends missing the final tokens. Only occurs when requests route through their Envoy gRPC gateway that translates to HTTP/1.1 upstream. Hitting our runtime directly (h2->h2) does not reproduce.

Mike R: Can you paste the minimal repro and their client logs? Curious whether this is a client-side reassembly bug or proxy-level rebuffering.

Priya S: Customer provided a tiny repro and a small Node fetch trace. Repro commands they used:
```
# direct to backend (works):
curl --http2 -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://runtime.redwood.internal/v1/stream?prompt=hello"

# through gateway (broken):
curl --http2 -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://gateway.acme/v1/stream?prompt=hello"
```
They report: when they intentionally abort the client (ctrl-c) and reconnect quickly, the gateway path sometimes splits the last SSE event into two separate events: e.g. first connection receives `data: \"Hello wor\"` and after reconnect the next event is `data: \"ld!\\n\\n\"`. With direct h2->h2 the event always arrives intact.

Alex K: This smells like codec translation + buffering. When proxies convert HTTP/2 streaming to HTTP/1.1 chunked responses they often wait for flush boundaries or coalesce small writes, which breaks SSE event atomicity. Two typical modes: (1) proxy buffers until it thinks it has a full chunk and then emits, so a single logical SSE event becomes multiple chunks across connections; (2) proxy closes the underlying http1 connection on a half-close and the remaining buffered bytes are sent as a new response on reconnect, leading to duplicates.

Alex K: Questions to narrow it down:
- On the gateway->upstream hop, is the response showing `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`?
- Is the gateway injecting or stripping `Content-Length`? That would force buffering.
- Are they terminating TLS/h2 at the gateway (i.e., gateway->upstream is http/1.1)?

Priya S: They confirmed the gateway terminates TLS/h2 and speaks HTTP/1.1 to our upstream. `Content-Length` is not present, but Envoy was configured with an http1 codec and default buffering.

Eli M: Operational mitigations we normally recommend for intermediaries:
- Avoid full buffering in the gateway. For nginx set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection ""; proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering no;`
- For Envoy prefer preserving http2 end-to-end. If translation is unavoidable, tune the HTTP connection manager to disable response buffering and make sure flushes are honored.
- On the server side, always terminate SSE events with `\\n\\n` and emit periodic SSE comments (e.g., `: keepalive\\n\\n`) every 15-30s to force proxy flushes.
- Add SSE `id:` fields and rely on Last-Event-ID/`id` resume semantics so clients can dedupe resumed fragments.

Priya S: Customer shared the gateway snippet (sanitized). They had left buffering at defaults:
```
location /v1/stream {
  proxy_pass http://upstream;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
  # proxy_buffering on  <-- default
}
```

Alex K: Yup, default buffering is the smoking gun. Nginx will spool small responses before forwarding; that kills streaming semantics. Recommend `proxy_buffering off; proxy_ignore_client_abort on;` and `add_header X-Accel-Buffering no;` so writes are flushed immediately.

Eli M: Additional checklist for the customer we should send:
1) Verify `Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` pass through unchanged.
2) Disable proxy buffering at the gateway (nginx/Envoy/GCP LB).
3) Where possible, preserve HTTP/2 end-to-end through the gateway.
4) Emit SSE `id:` and have client send `Last-Event-ID` to resume/dedupe.
5) Add server keepalives/comments to force flushes.
6) For Envoy, bump `stream_idle_timeout`/`idle_timeout` and ensure `max_stream_duration` not prematurely cutting streams.

Mike R: I'll package that checklist plus a short repro and ask them to try `curl -v --no-buffer --http2 -N` vs `curl --http2 -N` to compare. Also asked them to run a tcpdump between gateway and upstream so we can see chunk boundaries if they can share.

Priya S: Customer is rolling the gateway change now (disabling buffering). They also asked if Redwood can be more tolerant server-side.

Alex K: On our side we can harden a few things: always emit full SSE events with double newline, send optional keepalives, and document common proxy configs. We can't control third-party proxies but we can make our server-friendly to flush semantics and recommend `id`+resume.

EngOncall Bot: CI job queued: deploy/streaming-checker #112 — running a small test that simulates mid-event aborts against an envoy proxy.

Alex K: If the customer still sees split/tokens after disabling buffering, I'll spin up a minimal Envoy proxy with the same config and simulate random aborts with `wrk`/custom client to reproduce. If we can repro internally we'll look at mitigation code paths in the runtime to ensure periodic flushes and event finalization.

Priya S: Thanks all — I'll update once customer confirms whether disabling `proxy_buffering` fixed it. :thumbsup:
